the decrease of NO formation in kidney tissue detected by EPR in ARF induced by high-osmolar contrast media is prevented by simultaneous administration of calcium channel blocker.
the administration of calcium channel blocker verpamil prevented CM-induced acute renal failure and the decrease in NO formation in kidneys.

the possibility of using calcium channel blockers for the treatment of patients with ARF due to contrast media.
the role of calcium channel blockade in the prevention of CM-induced ARF.

the decrease in NO synthesis in kidney tissues is an important pathogenetic mechanism of CM-induced ARF, and verapamil may be a useful agent for prevention of this nephrotoxic effect of CM.

the protective effect of verampil in ARF due to CM is probably due to normalization of NO synthesis in renal tissues.
